messages:
incident-bot: ALERT: p99 latency breach in eu-dedicated cluster (eu-west-2). Metric: streaming p99 > 10s, p95 ~ 1.2s, error spikes on streaming sessions. Pager sent to @carlos (oncall).

carlos: seeing a lot of timeouts in the streaming router, p99s trending up for the last 8m. Most requests are hitting model-x-large on dedicated pools.

ana: tagging in — are these per-tenant bursts or system-wide? any correlated autoscale events?

carlos: initial look: queue depth on dedicated-eu-pool-3 jumped to 320 (normal ~20), autoscaler reports "insufficient capacity" for ~3min before failing to provision. A lot of cold KV cache misses too (spike in KV coldpath).

kevin: interesting — I see a batch job from customer_acme started ~10:12 and spawned 150 concurrent sessions to model-x-large. That knocked over the pool. Autoscaler evaluated capacity but rejected because the warmup window policy considered recent idle latency and refused burst add.

julia: so autoscaler misjudged due to percentile smoothing? ops-bot logs show a smoothed avg latency low -> failed to predict sudden burst.

carlos: impact: several enterprise customers on dedicated pools saw partial streams (clients got initial tokens then stall), some retried which amplified queue depth. Nava (support) reports two customers opened tickets about truncated responses.

ana: customer impact severity? any SLA hits?

carlos: p99 latency breach = SLO breach for eu dedicated tier. I'm going to page infra-sre and spin emergency nodes. Starting mitigation steps now.

kevin: mitigation proposal in order: 1) temporarily route non-enterprise traffic to hosted fallback small-model (model-x-small) 2) evict large KV caches and clear cache to free memory 3) manually scale up pool with immediate warmup bypass (emergency flag) 4) apply ingress token-level throttles for batchy customers.

julia: +1 for throttles. If we spin nodes without warming KV caches we'll still see coldpath penalties. Need to pre-warm key prefixes used by streaming router. I can push a warmup script.

carlos: executing now. Runbook commands:
```
# immediate emergency scale
infractl pools scale dedicated-eu-pool-3 --replicas 10 --bypass-warn
# clear KV cache safely
redis-cli -h kv-eu-3 FLUSHDB --pattern model-x-large:*
# route rule
routectl set fallback-route --from dedicated-eu-pool-3 --to hosted-model-x-small --percent 40
```

ops-bot: ACTION_LOG: manual scale triggered by carlos @ 1769995568. Cache flush job queued. Route change pending approval.

nora: pushed warmup script to the pool, will prefetch top 200 key prefixes used by streaming router. Script logs: warming 50/200... 100/200...

kevin: I'm throttling customer_acme to 20rps (soft limit) to stop noisy neighbor. Also contacting account manager to warn.

carlos: route change applied -> 40% traffic shifted. p95 improved to 850ms after partial reroute, p99 down to ~3.1s but still above SLO. Queue depth falling from 320 -> 120.

julia: warmup complete for top prefixes. Observed KV coldpath miss rate drop from 78% -> 18% on those prefixes.

carlos: autoscaler logs show it previously rejected scale due to a bug in burst-detection that used a 5m sliding window; the sudden burst from the batch job fooled it. Filing bug: AUTOSCALE-2319.

ana: we should consider a fast-path emergency scale policy for Dedicated pools when queue depth > 200 and streaming p99 > 5s. Add to playbook.

kevin: agree. Also recommend adding tenant-level backpressure: detect rapid session count increase from single tenant and apply token bucket.

ops-bot: INCIDENT_UPDATE: p99 back within 1.1s for 90% of routes; remaining tail at ~2.8s. Customer tickets updated, support notified.

carlos: manual scale now stable, pool at target replicas. Applying post-mortem steps: lock down batch job scheduling policy for high-impact tenants, roll out autoscaler patch to adjust smoothing window and add a burst bypass flag.

julia: note for follow-up: evaluate KV eviction strategy — large-model caches should have a separate eviction priority so warmup can be quicker.

nora: support notes: two customers saw truncated streams — workaround was to hit fallback hosted endpoint or retry with backoff. Sent escalation guidance to support team.

ana: preparing incident summary and severity = sev2 (SLO breach, partial degradation, manual mitigation). Will add timeline and mitigation metrics.

kevin: I've reached out to account team for customers impacted, and flagged potential billing credits if needed.

carlos: handing off to @ana for long-running remediation and postmortem owner. Next oncall please monitor dedicated-eu-pool-3 for 4h.

ana: taking ownership for postmortem, will coordinate with runtime and autoscale teams. Action items captured: [AUTOSCALE-2319], [POOL-WARMUP-42], [KV-EVICT-87], throttle rule RFC.

incident-bot: INCIDENT RESOLVED: primary mitigations applied and p99 within acceptable SLO for majority of customers. Incident closed for live paging at 1769995622.

carlos: thanks everyone — add any lingering notes in the postmortem doc and tag me for follow-ups. :thumbsup:
